'''Masato Sagawa''' (佐川眞人; born August 3, 1943, in [[Tokushima]], [[Japan]]) is a Japanese scientist and entrepreneur, and the inventor of the [[sintered]] permanent [[neodymium magnet]] (NdFeB). 
Sagawa was awarded the [[Japan Prize]] and [[IEEE Medal for Environmental and Safety Technologies]] for his efforts.

== Career ==
Sagawa initially conceived and developed the sintered NdFeB when he was with [[Fujitsu]] Laboratories, where he worked from 1972 to 1982. Lacking his supervisor's support for the new magnetic compound, Sagawa resigned in 1981,  joining [[Sumitomo Metal Industries|Sumitomo Special Metals]]. Shortly after joining Sumitomo he had developed the NdFeB magnet. Sagawa presented the new discovery of NdFeB magnet during the Magnetism and Magnetic Materials Conference in November 1983 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.<ref name="M. Sagawa, S. Fujimura 1984">{{cite journal |last1=Sagawa |first1=M. |last2=Fujimura |first2=S. |last3=Togawa |first3=N. |last4=Yamamoto |first4=H. |last5=Matsuura |first5=Y. |title=New material for permanent magnets on a base of Nd and Fe (invited) |journal=Journal of Applied Physics |date=1984 |volume=55 |issue=6 |pages=2083–2087 |doi=10.1063/1.333572}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Sagawa|first1=M.|last2=Fujimura|first2=S.|last3=Yamamoto|first3=H.|last4=Matsuura|first4=Y.|last5=Hiraga|first5=K.|title=Permanent magnet materials based on the rare earth-iron-boron tetragonal compounds|journal=IEEE Transactions on Magnetics|date=September 1984|volume=20|issue=5|pages=1584–1589|doi=10.1109/TMAG.1984.1063214|citeseerx=10.1.1.533.8984}}</ref> During this same time period, John Croat from [[General Motors]] (GM) had independently discovered the same Nd<sub>2</sub>Fe<sub>14</sub>B compound.<ref name="Lucas">{{ cite book | last1  = Lucas | first1 = Jacques | last2  = Lucas | first2 =  Pierre | last3  = Le Mercier | first3 = Thierry | last4  = Rollat | first4 = Alain | last5  = Davenport | first5 = William | title  = Rare Earths: Science, Technology, Production and Use | publisher = Elsevier | date   = 2014 | pages  = 224–225 | url    = https://books.google.com/books?id=y0Z9AwAAQBAJ&q=neodymium&pg=PA224 | isbn   = 978-0-444-62744-5 | display-authors = 3 }}</ref>

In 1988, Sagawa founded Intermetallics, a research and development company devoted to the development of [[neodymium magnet]]s.<ref name="O. Gutfleisch, J.P. Liu 2011">{{cite journal|last1=Gutfleisch|first1=Oliver|last2=Willard|first2=Matthew A.|last3=Brück|first3=Ekkes|last4=Chen|first4=Christina H.|last5=Sankar|first5=S. G.|last6=Liu|first6=J. Ping|title=Magnetic Materials and Devices for the 21st Century: Stronger, Lighter, and More Energy Efficient|journal=Advanced Materials|date=15 February 2011|volume=23|issue=7|pages=821–842|doi=10.1002/adma.201002180|pmid=21294168}}</ref><ref name=jp2>{{cite web|title=Achievement : Developing the world's highest performing Nd-Fe-B type permanent magnet and contributing to energy conservation|url=http://www.japanprize.jp/data/prize/2012/e_2_achievements.pdf|website=The Japan Prize Foundation|accessdate=29 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Changing the EV and the World with the Motor|url=http://www.mitsubishicorp.com/jp/en/mclibrary/business/vol1/page5.html|website=Mitsubishi Corp|accessdate=29 July 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151008232119/http://www.mitsubishicorp.com/jp/en/mclibrary/business/vol1/page5.html|archivedate=8 October 2015}}</ref>  Sagawa founded NDFEB Corporation in 2012, where he is currently president. 

Sagawa has worked on improving the NdFeB magnetic materials' magnetic properties, with over 60 patents for his work related to NdFeB. The 2022 [[Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering]] was awarded to him for the discovery, development and global commercialisation of the neodymium-iron-boron (Nd-Fe-B) magnet.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-60205351 |title=Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering honours magnet pioneer |publisher=BBC News |date=1 February 2022}}</ref>

*2024 - [[European Inventor Award]]
*2026 - [[Person of Cultural Merit]]<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUD229PH0S6A021C2000000/|script-title=ja:文化勲章・功労者の業績と略歴 2026年度|access-date= October 23, 2026|date= October 23, 2026|website= The Nikkei|language=ja}}</ref>
